subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Find the number of ways of selecting an 11-member cricket team from 7 batsmen, 6 bowlers and 2 wicket keepers so that the team contains 2 wicket keepers and at least 4 bowlers.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the teams — which compositions are allowed, how each is counted, and how you finish.
insider_note: Both keepers are in the team from the start, so only 9 places remain and the batsmen count is 9 − bowlers, never 11 − bowlers. Write the bowler cases 4, 5, 6 as a table first — the list of compositions is a mark on its own.

steps.label: List the allowed compositions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both keepers are in every team (²C₂ = 1), so 9 places remain for bowlers and batsmen. Bowlers can be 4, 5 or 6; the batsmen make up 9.
lines: Both wicket keepers are in the team: ²C₂ = 1.
The other 9 places: at least 4 bowlers,
so bowlers 4, 5 or 6 with batsmen 5, 4 or 3.

recall.must_convey: That the two keepers are fixed, and the remaining nine places split as 4, 5 or 6 bowlers with 5, 4 or 3 batsmen.
accept: both keepers are taken, then nine places with four five or six bowlers and five four or three batsmen
three cases, four bowlers five batsmen, five and four, six and three, plus the two keepers
two C two is one for the keepers and then the bowlers are at least four so three cases
keepers iddaru fix, migatha nine lo bowlers four five or six, batsmen five four three
list the cases by number of bowlers, four five and six

steps.why: Fixing the keepers first turns an 11-place problem into a 9-place one. The bowler count then runs from the minimum 4 up to all 6, and each value is a separate, non-overlapping case.
common_mistakes: Treating the keepers as a choice of 1 or 2 — the question says the team contains 2.
Stopping at 5 bowlers and missing the 6-bowler case.

steps.label: Count each composition
steps.margin_note: Two marks. ⁶C₄ = ⁶C₂ = 15, ⁷C₅ = ⁷C₂ = 21, ⁷C₄ = ⁷C₃ = 35. Multiply within each case.

recall.must_convey: That each case multiplies keepers, bowlers and batsmen — 315, 210 and 35.
accept: six C four times seven C five is three hundred fifteen, six C five times seven C four is two hundred ten, six C six times seven C three is thirty five
multiply the three selections in each case to get three fifteen, two ten and thirty five
the cases give three hundred and fifteen, two hundred and ten and thirty five
prathi case lo keepers bowlers batsmen multiply cheste three fifteen, two ten, thirty five
fifteen times twenty one, six times thirty five, one times thirty five

steps.why: Within a case the three groups are chosen together, so their counts multiply. ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ keeps the arithmetic small: ⁷C₅ is ⁷C₂, not a product of five numbers.
common_mistakes: Adding the selections inside a case instead of multiplying.
Using ⁷C₅ = 35 — that is ⁷C₃; ⁷C₅ = 21.
Leaving out the batsmen factor in the 6-bowler case; ⁷C₃ = 35 is still needed.

steps.label: Add the cases

recall.must_convey: That the three case counts are added to give 560.
accept: add three fifteen, two ten and thirty five to get five hundred sixty
the total is five hundred and sixty
adding the three cases gives five sixty
moodu cases add cheste five hundred sixty
three hundred fifteen plus two hundred ten plus thirty five is five sixty

steps.why: Teams with different numbers of bowlers are different teams, so the cases are disjoint and adding them counts every team exactly once.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the cases instead of adding.
Adding only two of the three cases.
